Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray shows marked elevation of the right hemidiaphragm, which is a classic sign of right diaphragmatic paralysis (often due to phrenic nerve injury), while the scalloped or wavy appearance of the left hemidiaphragm is a common normal anatomical variant (diaphragmatic eventration or normal contour) and not indicative of pathology in this context.
